svg.text: Bows and crossbows — the looks (CE-1976, BW-3 / BW-10)

Scope (R-4151): ONLY the bow, crossbow, quiver / bolt case, arrow, bolt, stuck arrow and the draw pose. The grey figure, the horse, the wall and the ground are the existing looks, drawn for context and unchanged.
1 · Archer aiming — the bow drawn to the cheek
bow arm straight out to the grip, the string hand at the cheek, elbow raised
and out;
the arrow nocked: shaft, metal point, two crossed red vanes. From his left, and
from behind.
side (from his left)
from behind
2 · Archer carrying — bow in the left hand, quiver on the back
at ease / ready: the stave hangs upright at his side, its string toward his
body (a plane facing out);
no arrow in hand. The quiver slants from the right hip to over the left
shoulder, three fletchings showing.
front
side (stave edge-on)
3 · Crossbowman — stock, prod, spanned string, bolt
a wooden stock along the rifle's line; a prod of two swept limbs across its
front; the string spanned back
to a catch; a short thick bolt on the rail. A short leather bolt case at the
right hip (no quiver).
side
from above (prod swept back)
4 · Warrior on his horse — bow in hand, quiver on his back
the same type mounts the riding horse (703) and draws the bow from the saddle
(BW-8); the hips sit
on the horse's back, the legs round the barrel. Horse and rider's legs are the
existing looks.
side — drawn
5 · The arrow in flight (MunitionShape.Arrow) — and the bolt
a slim shaft, a metal point, THREE vanes round the tail; the nose along the
velocity, so it pitches over its arc.
A bolt is the same shape, shorter (0.40 m) and thicker (Ø 10 mm), its vanes
shorter and dark. Arrow 0.75 m × Ø 8 mm.
arrow — 0.75 m
crossbow bolt — 0.40 m
end-on: three vanes at 120°
flight → the point leads; no tumble (unlike the thrown axe)
6 · Arrows stuck in a wall and in the ground
lying + Sticks (BW-4): drawn along the round's replicated rotation at its
replicated place — NOT flat;
its point already a third of its length inside the surface (backend sets the
position), the shaft sticking out.
wall
ground
wall, 12° down
wall, 8° up
ground, 30°
ground, steep
dashed = the part inside the surface (a third); drawn in 3-D by the surface hiding it
7 · The thrown tomahawk — the existing axe look (CE-1190)
his hatchet munition (TkbThrowingHatchet) is already MunitionShape.Axe: a haft
with a head block and a blade, tumbling end over end
in flight, flat on the ground when it lies (rails: CE1190_ThrownBlades_…).
Nothing to build.
8 · Where each look lives, and how it is chosen
• HeldLook.Bow / Crossbow — WeaponCategory.Bow (14); the mount's round says which (an arrow ⇒ Bow, a bolt ⇒ Crossbow); BlockFigure.BowHeld reshapes the arms and
appends the stave / string / arrow parts.
• the quiver / bolt case — torso details of a man who holds a bow / crossbow; they follow every stance (crouch, prone, seated, mounted).
• the draw pose — when his weapon posture is Aimed; carried (left hand, string toward him) at ease / ready and when prone. A rider's bow is drawn when he fires
(the firing seat).
• the arrow in flight — ProjectileLayer.SolidsOf, MunitionShape.Arrow (shaft + point + 3 vanes); the stuck arrow — the replicated rotation (StuckNose), not lifted
onto the ground, not flat.
• a nocked arrow is drawn 0.66 m long (the figure's draw length), not the flying arrow's 0.75 m — one deviation, named in the design's as-built.
